title: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve
capsule: The Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve (Arabic: Shantamariyyat al-Gharb; capital at modern Faro) was a small Harunid principality in the southernmost Iberian Peninsula, one of the successor states that emerged from the collapse of the Caliphate of Córdoba after 1031. Sa'id ibn Harun ruled from approximately 1018 until his death c. 1041, followed by his son Muhammad al-Mu'tasim. The Abbadid ruler Abbad II al-Mu'tadid of Seville conquered the taifa around 1051, adding it to his expanding southern domain; the region remained under Sevillian and later Almoravid control until the Portuguese Reconquista reached Faro in 1249.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The taifa's core around Faro is secure from Islamic chronicle sources; its northern hinterland boundaries are not well defined in contemporary documents and are reconstructed by analogy with later administrative divisions.
